legend: You are given an array of positive integers. While there are at least two equal elements, we will perform the following operation. We choose the smallest value x%%ZSMJ0%% that occurs in the array 2%%ZSMJ1%% or more times. Take the first two occurrences of x%%ZSMJ2%% in this array (the two leftmost occurrences). Remove the left of these two occurrences, and the right one is replaced by the sum of this two values (that is, 2⋅x%%ZSMJ3%%).
Determine how the array will look after described operations are performed.
For example, consider the given array looks like [3,4,1,2,2,1,1]%%ZSMJ4%%. It will be changed in the following way: [3,4,1,2,2,1,1] → [3,4,2,2,2,1] → [3,4,4,2,1] → [3,8,2,1]%%ZSMJ5%%.
If the given array is look like [1,1,3,1,1]%%ZSMJ6%% it will be changed in the following way: [1,1,3,1,1] → [2,3,1,1] → [2,3,2] → [3,4]%%ZSMJ7%%.
input: The first line contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ8%% (2≤n≤150000%%ZSMJ9%%) — the number of elements in the array.
The second line contains a sequence from n%%ZSMJ10%% elements a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ11%% (1≤ai≤109%%ZSMJ12%%) — the elements of the array.
output: In the first line print an integer k%%ZSMJ13%% — the number of elements in the array after all the performed operations. In the second line print k%%ZSMJ14%% integers — the elements of the array after all the performed operations.
note: The first two examples were considered in the statement.
In the third example all integers in the given array are distinct, so it will not change.
